newsitem.title: USA: Dow Chemical wins silicone implant ruling.
newsitem.headline: Dow Chemical wins silicone implant ruling.

text.p: Dow Chemical Co. said Monday it won an important victory in its battle against breast-implant litigation -- a federal appeals court ruling that it is not liable for injury claims by recipients of Dow Corning silicone jaw implants.

Dow Chemical said the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit in St. Paul, Minn., on Friday upheld a lower court ruling dismissing it from all federal lawsuits involving silicone temporomandibular joint implants.
The implants were once marketed by Dow Corning, a 50-50 joint venture between Dow Chemical and Corning Inc.

Dow Corning also was once the nation's largest maker of silicone-gel breast implants and has been in bankruptcy court for two years trying to deal with claims from thousands of women that the implants caused various illnesses, including lupus, rheumatoid arthritis and connective tissue diseases.

The bankruptcy proceedings have effectively frozen litigation against Dow Corning, so many plaintiffs have filed claims against Dow Chemical, citing silicone-worker safety testing the company did on behalf of Dow Corning in the 1940s and 1950s.

The appeals court ruled that the testing did not constitute legal grounds for holding Dow Chemical directly liable for the plaintiffs' alleged injuries. The jaw implants were prescribed to alleviate pain and correct improper functioning of the joint connecting the upper and lower jaw.

Dow Chemical has long maintained that it never tested, made or sold any medical implants and that it was never notified by Dow Corning that any of the silicone compounds it tested would be used in implants.

A U.S. District Court judge in Detroit heard arguments Monday on whether she should allow a class-action breast implant trial against Dow Chemical to proceed in New Orleans. Judge Denise Page Hood delayed a decision, keeping the two-month old trial in limbo.
The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit in Cincinnati ruled May 9 that all breast implant cases naming Dow Chemical and Corning Inc. as defendants be consolidated in federal court in Detroit.

Dow Chemical general counsel John Scriven said that Friday's appeals ruling was a "major finding reflecting a maturing legal consensus that there is no basis in the law or the facts for Dow Chemical to be in the silicone litigation.
"The Eighth Circuit ruling is consistent with Dow's dismissal from some 4,000 silicone-gel breast implant cases in New York, California and Michigan," Scriven said.
Dow Chemical's stock lost $1 to $86.375 on the New York Stock Exchange.
